mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-41.6 to -31.6), indicating an established recovery momentum that is likely to persist by simple trend continuation, pushing the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -41.6 to -31.6 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the prior 28-day mean despite three consecutive weeks of prior improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has fallen four consecutive weeks (17.9 to 13.9). Once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 14-point threshold, households are spending materially less time at home, which should translate into increased out-of-home retail and recreation activity within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 17.9 to 13.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days does not rise relative to the prior 14 days even after RESIDENTIAL crosses below 14.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES (-38.6 to -28.9) and TRANSIT (-56.9 to -48.7) signals a joint commuting-and-transit recovery; when both rise together, the combined effect on retail footfall is amplified beyond either series alone because workers both leave home and use public transit to reach commercial areas, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue improving concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has nearly returned to baseline (-0.9), indicating essential-sector restrictions have been substantially relaxed under a reopening policy regime; this signals broader retail-sector reopening is imminent and will lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as non-essential retail categories follow the same policy relaxation path.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days remains flat or declines even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above -2.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dipped sharply at t-2w (-36.6) then partially rebounded to -28.3, consistent with a mid-spring seasonal pattern of increasing outdoor activity; as warmer weather continues this will substitute for retail trips in the very short term, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next week before recovering.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated between -36.6 and -26.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite PARKS mobility remaining elevated or increasing further.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT usage has improved markedly but remains deeply suppressed (-48.7); once TRANSIT crosses above -45 it signals a critical mass of commuters returning to public transport, which historically precedes a surge in downtown and commercial-district retail visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -56.9 to -48.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following TRANSIT crossing above -45.0.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM nears baseline while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, households satisfy essential needs locally but have not resumed broader discretionary outings; this divergence pattern indicates discretionary retail recovery is lagging and will keep RETAIL_REC growth muted over the next two weeks until WORKPLACES also recovers meaningfully.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM within 5 points of baseline while WORKPLACES remains below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days by more than 3 points despite this divergence persisting between GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If local authorities have not yet lifted retail-specific closures (inferred from RETAIL_REC remaining far below GROCERY_PHARM's near-baseline level), the gap itself signals an active policy restriction specific to non-essential retail; under this restrictive regime, RETAIL_REC is capped and will not meaningfully increase over the next four weeks regardless of other mobility improvements.
candidate_trigger: gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC exceeds 25 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -31.6 vs GROCERY_PHARM at -0.9, a gap of 30.7 points
regime_hint: tightening or partial restrictions on non-essential retail
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean rises by more than 5 points over the next 28 days even while the GROCERY_PHARM-RETAIL_REC gap remains above 25 points.
